**Discpress 1.2.0 tunes itself to your device.** Instead of guessing how many processor cores to use, Discpress now measures your phone, tablet or computer once and creates CHDs with the number of threads that is actually fastest on it. There's nothing to set up.

## Download

**[⬇ discpress.html](https://github.com/PowerBeef/discpress/releases/download/v1.2.0/discpress.html)** (about 2.7 MB). The whole app in one file that works offline. To update, download it and use it instead of your old copy.

## What's new

### Automatic speed tuning

The first time you create a CHD, the progress bar shows **"Measuring this device's speed (only once)…"** for a few seconds. Discpress compresses some test data with 1, 2, 3, 4… threads and keeps the fastest. Every later conversion uses that result straight away.

- **Recent devices get more out of their chips.** Some browsers report fewer cores than the device really has. The speed test doesn't rely on that number, so recent Apple silicon Macs and iPads, iPhones, and Snapdragon laptops and phones can use every core that helps.
- **Older devices are looked after too.** If extra threads don't make things faster, for example on a phone that would only get hot, Discpress uses fewer. Before the first test it starts from the same settings as before.
- **Updates are noticed.** When your browser updates, Discpress measures again the next time.

### You're still in control

**Settings → CPU threads for compression** now defaults to **Automatic (recommended)** and shows what was measured on your device. **Measure again** runs the test again, which is handy after closing other heavy apps. You can still pick a fixed number of threads, and then Discpress skips the test. **Diagnostics** now lists the speed at each thread count tested.

## Same files as desktop chdman

Your CHDs are still exactly the same, byte for byte, as the ones desktop chdman 0.289 makes, however many threads are used. Every change in this release was checked against it with the automated test suite.
